classification.difficultyReason: Model interior and border tile counts, complete a product in two variables, justify admissible factor signs and convert all factor pairs into whole-tiling dimensions.

content.prompt: The tiling below consists of a rectangle of orange square tiles, with a border of blue square tiles that is one tile wide. We want to make a similar tiling for which the number of orange tiles is twice the number of blue tiles. Find all possible lengths and widths of such tilings.

spec.description: Seven columns and four rows of equal square tiles, with a five-column by two-row orange interior and a complete blue border. TikZ preserves two distinct tile classes, which a single-shade fraction-grid template cannot express.
spec.mathematics: 10 interior tiles and 18 border tiles; border thickness is one tile.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied illustration is always visible and contains no requested dimensions.

answer.short:
Whole tiling dimensions, in tile widths: $7\times30,\ 8\times18,\ 9\times14,\ 10\times12$, allowing rotation.

The corresponding orange rectangles are $5\times28,\ 6\times16,\ 7\times12,\ 8\times10$. Grouping gives $(m-4)(n-4)=24$ for orange-region dimensions $m,n$.
answer.worked:
Let the orange rectangle have dimensions $m\times n$ tiles. Its blue border contains
$$\begin{align*}(m+2)(n+2)-mn&=mn+2m+2n+4-mn\\(m+2)(n+2)-mn&=2m+2n+4.
\end{align*}$$
The required count condition gives
$$\begin{align*}mn&=2(2m+2n+4)\\mn-4m-4n&=8\\mn-4m-4n+16&=24\\m(n-4)-4(n-4)&=24\\(m-4)(n-4)&=24.
\end{align*}$$
Positive $m,n$ cannot both be below $4$, since then $(m-4)(n-4)\le9$. Thus both factors are positive. Up to rotation, the factor pairs are $(1,24),(2,12),(3,8),(4,6)$.
The orange-region dimensions are $5\times28,\ 6\times16,\ 7\times12,\ 8\times10$.
Adding the one-tile border on both sides gives whole tiling dimensions $7\times30,\ 8\times18,\ 9\times14,\ 10\times12$ tile widths.
